summary:
Workplace Insight promotes Work in Motion, a six-part documentary podcast series written and presented by Ian Ellison and produced by Dave Crackles, which follows the making of Work Beyond Walls, a new workplace event at the Grade II listed Boiler Shop in Newcastle on 9 and 10 September. The framing argument is that the workplace sector mostly publishes content after outcomes are known: case studies appear once a move-in has succeeded, award entries once risks are mitigated, producing a library of polished endings. The podcast instead documents an attempt while the outcome remains uncertain.

Work Beyond Walls is the idea of Paul Glaister, co-founder of Gateshead-based workspace interiors and design business Workpattern. He booked the venue, part of the former Robert Stephenson and Company site where Rocket was built, before the event had a name, brand, website, speaker, budget or a single registration. Philippa Lobb, Workpattern's newest recruit, canvassed regional architects and designers; Beth Lawford, an interior designer at GT3 Architects who returned to Newcastle after working at Gensler and Fletcher Priest in London, suggested filling a railway arch near the station with furniture for a couple of days.

The event now involves over twenty brand partners, a talks programme and a real-time data insights experiment, and is positioned as neither an expo, trade show nor conference. Glaister calls it the North East's first living workplace event, where the building becomes a free-to-attend workspace visitors can work from across two days. His motivation is escaping industry self-talk and reaching beyond the sector bubble.

Workpattern commissioned the podcast on the basis that it would not be a glossy advert and registration numbers would not be hidden. When recording began in July there was one registration against a target of 500; by episode two, sign-ups had risen but remained well short. Episode two features Herb Kim, Dave James, Terry McStea, Katie Richardson, Will Easton and Mark Eltringham.

claims.claim: Work Beyond Walls had one registration against a target of five hundred when podcast recording began in July
